title: Distinguish transformer families, pretraining and adaptation, inference context, and sparse-expert routing without equating fluent output with verified reasoning

questions.prompt:
Two pretrained transformers are compared for writing open-ended text, such as continuing a story from a prompt:

- **Model A** is decoder-only. It was pretrained on next-token prediction with a causal attention mask, so each position attends only to earlier tokens.
- **Model B** is encoder-only. It was pretrained on masked-token prediction with bidirectional attention: some input tokens are hidden, and each position can attend to tokens on both sides.

Model B could still be forced to produce text, for example by appending a mask token, predicting it and repeating. Explain why Model A's pretraining directly trains the step used to continue a prompt, while Model B's pretraining does not.

rubric.point: Model A: the causal mask plus next-token objective trains the model to predict the next token from the preceding prefix only. That is the same step used at generation time (predict, append, repeat), so training and autoregressive generation match.

Model B: masked-token pretraining trains it to fill in hidden tokens within a sequence, typically using context on both sides, and it outputs contextual representations for a task head. It is never trained to repeatedly extend a prefix and has no autoregressive decoder, so any append-and-predict loop runs outside its training setup. Credit any answer conveying this training mismatch; do not require a claim that generation is impossible.

questions.model:
**Model A:** The causal mask means each position predicts the next token from earlier tokens only. Generation uses exactly that step: predict the next token, append it and repeat. Pretraining therefore directly trains the continuation path.

**Model B:** It was trained to fill in masked tokens inside a sequence, usually with context on both sides, and to produce contextual representations for a task head. It was never trained to extend a prefix one token at a time and has no autoregressive decoder. A loop that appends and predicts masks can run, but it differs from how the model was trained, so it is not a reliable way to generate open-ended text.
